newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes further up on T-bill buying. [corrected 14:50 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes further up on T-bill buying. [corrected 14:50 gmt]

text.p: The Bulgarian lev gained further to 1,695-1,700 (corrects from 1,965-1,700) per dollar at close from midday's 1,700-1,704 as foreign investors sold foreign currency for levs to lock into high-yielding government securities, dealers said.

* Foreign investors were actively selling foreign currency for levs to buy discount T-bills in anticipation of a sharp fall in interest rates on lev-denominated instruments under a currency board system, to be launched from July 1.
* Foreign currency demand was low in the afternoon as most bidders were out of the market.

* The lev opened at 1,705-1,715 per dollar, down from Friday's close at 1,690-1,694 as banks and clients were bidding for foreign currency to meet pending payments and build up positions ahead of a 1,000 levs-per-mark peg under the currency board.
* The lev closed at 979-982 per mark, a touch stronger the opening's 980-985, tracking the international mark/dollar cross. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
